passages.text: Now it pleased Darius to appoint 120 satraps to rule throughout the kingdom, and over them three administrators, including Daniel, to whom these satraps were accountable so that the king would not suffer loss.
passages.sermon:
Darius became king.
Darius was sixty-two years old.
Darius ruled over the kingdom.
Darius decided to appoint officials.
Darius appointed 120 satraps.
These satraps ruled throughout the whole kingdom.
Darius also appointed three administrators over the satraps.
Daniel was one of these three administrators.
The satraps reported to the administrators.
The administrators made sure the king would not suffer loss.
passages.original: שְׁפַר֙ קֳדָ֣ם דָּרְיָ֔וֶשׁ וַהֲקִים֙ עַל־ מַלְכוּתָ֔א לַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֖א מְאָ֣ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֑ין דִּ֥י לֶהֱוֺ֖ן בְּכָל־ מַלְכוּתָֽא׃ וְעֵ֤לָּא מִנְּהוֹן֙ סָרְכִ֣ין תְּלָתָ֔א דִּ֥י דָנִיֵּ֖אל חַֽד־ מִנְּה֑וֹן דִּֽי־ לֶהֱוֺ֞ן אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֗ין יָהֲבִ֤ין לְהוֹן֙ טַעְמָ֔א וּמַלְכָּ֖א לָֽא־ לֶהֱוֵ֥א נָזִֽק׃

passages.text: Soon, by his extraordinary spirit, Daniel distinguished himself among the administrators and satraps. So the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was one of the three main administrators under King Darius.
Daniel had an extraordinary spirit.
Daniel stood out among all the administrators and satraps.
Daniel performed better than the others.
King Darius noticed Daniel’s excellence.
The king decided to put Daniel in charge of the whole kingdom.
passages.original: אֱדַ֙יִן֙ דָּנִיֵּ֣אל דְּנָ֔ה הֲוָ֣א מִתְנַצַּ֔ח עַל־ סָרְכַיָּ֖א וַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֑א כָּל־ קֳבֵ֗ל דִּ֣י ר֤וּחַ יַתִּירָא֙ בֵּ֔הּ וּמַלְכָּ֣א עֲשִׁ֔ית לַהֲקָמוּתֵ֖הּ עַל־ כָּל־ מַלְכוּתָֽא׃

passages.text: Thus the administrators and satraps sought a charge against Daniel concerning the kingdom, but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was one of three administrators over the kingdom of Darius.
Darius appointed Daniel because Daniel had an extraordinary spirit.
The king planned to set Daniel over the whole kingdom.
The other administrators and satraps became jealous of Daniel.
They tried to find a reason to accuse Daniel concerning his work for the kingdom.
They searched for a charge or corruption against Daniel.
They could not find any charge against him.
They could not find any corruption in him.
Daniel was trustworthy.
Daniel was not negligent.
Daniel was not corrupt.
No fault or corruption was found in Daniel.
passages.original: אֱדַ֨יִן סָֽרְכַיָּ֜א וַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֗א הֲו֨וֹ בָעַ֧יִן עִלָּ֛ה לְהַשְׁכָּחָ֥ה לְדָנִיֵּ֖אל מִצַּ֣ד מַלְכוּתָ֑א וְכָל־ עִלָּ֨ה וּשְׁחִיתָ֜ה לָא־ יָכְלִ֣ין לְהַשְׁכָּחָ֗ה כָּל־ קֳבֵל֙ דִּֽי־ מְהֵימַ֣ן ה֔וּא וְכָל־ שָׁלוּ֙ וּשְׁחִיתָ֔ה לָ֥א הִשְׁתְּכַ֖חַת עֲלֽוֹהִי׃

passages.text: Finally these men said, “We will never find any charge against this Daniel, unless we find something against him concerning the law of his God.”
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a trustworthy man.
Daniel served under King Darius.
Daniel had no fault or corruption.
The administrators and satraps tried to find a charge against Daniel.
They could not find any fault in him.
They spoke together.
They said, "We will not find any charge against Daniel."
"We can only find something against him concerning the law of his God."
passages.original: אֱ֠דַיִן גֻּבְרַיָּ֤א אִלֵּךְ֙ אָֽמְרִ֔ין דִּ֣י לָ֧א נְהַשְׁכַּ֛ח לְדָנִיֵּ֥אל דְּנָ֖ה כָּל־ עִלָּ֑א לָהֵ֕ן הַשְׁכַּ֥חְנָֽה עֲל֖וֹהִי בְּדָ֥ת אֱלָהֵֽהּ׃ס

passages.text: So the administrators and satraps went together to the king and said, “O King Darius, may you live forever!
passages.sermon:
The administrators and satraps were officials in the kingdom.
They went together to the king.
They spoke to King Darius.
They said, “O King Darius, may you live forever!”
passages.original: אֱ֠דַיִן סָרְכַיָּ֤א וַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּא֙ אִלֵּ֔ן הַרְגִּ֖שׁוּ עַל־ מַלְכָּ֑א וְכֵן֙ אָמְרִ֣ין לֵ֔הּ דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֖א לְעָלְמִ֥ין חֱיִֽי׃

passages.text: All the royal administrators, prefects, satraps, advisers, and governors have agreed that the king should establish an ordinance and enforce a decree that for thirty days anyone who petitions any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.
passages.sermon:
The royal administrators, prefects, satraps, advisers, and governors met together.
They agreed on a plan.
They wanted the king to make a law.
They wanted the king to enforce a decree.
The law would last for thirty days.
The law said that anyone who prayed to any god or any person except the king would be punished.
The punishment was to be thrown into the den of lions.
passages.original: אִתְיָעַ֜טוּ כֹּ֣ל׀ סָרְכֵ֣י מַלְכוּתָ֗א סִגְנַיָּ֤א וַֽאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּא֙ הַדָּֽבְרַיָּ֣א וּפַחֲוָתָ֔א לְקַיָּמָ֤ה קְיָם֙ מַלְכָּ֔א וּלְתַקָּפָ֖ה אֱסָ֑ר דִּ֣י כָל־ דִּֽי־ יִבְעֵ֣ה בָ֠עוּ מִן־ כָּל־ אֱלָ֨הּ וֶֽאֱנָ֜שׁ עַד־ יוֹמִ֣ין תְּלָתִ֗ין לָהֵן֙ מִנָּ֣ךְ מַלְכָּ֔א יִתְרְמֵ֕א לְגֹ֖ב אַרְיָוָתָֽא׃

passages.text: Therefore, O king, establish the decree and sign the document so that it cannot be changed—in accordance with the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed.”
passages.sermon:
King Darius ruled the Medes and Persians.
The law of the Medes and Persians cannot be changed.
The administrators and officials spoke to King Darius.
They asked him to make a decree.
They told him to sign a written law.
They said the law must not be changed.
They said the law must follow the custom of the Medes and Persians.
They said the law must not be repealed.
passages.original: כְּעַ֣ן מַלְכָּ֔א תְּקִ֥ים אֱסָרָ֖א וְתִרְשֻׁ֣ם כְּתָבָ֑א דִּ֣י לָ֧א לְהַשְׁנָיָ֛ה כְּדָת־ מָדַ֥י וּפָרַ֖ס דִּי־ לָ֥א תֶעְדֵּֽא׃

passages.text: Therefore King Darius signed the written decree.
passages.sermon: King Darius was the ruler.\r\nHe signed the written decree.\r\nHe made the law official.
passages.original: כָּל־ קֳבֵ֖ל דְּנָ֑ה מַלְכָּא֙ דָּֽרְיָ֔וֶשׁ רְשַׁ֥ם כְּתָבָ֖א וֶאֱסָרָֽא׃

passages.text: Now when Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went into his house, where the windows of his upper room opened toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he got down on his knees, prayed, and gave thanks to his God, just as he had done before.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a Jewish exile in Babylon.
Daniel learned that King Darius had signed the decree.
This decree forbade prayer to anyone except the king.
Daniel went into his house.
His upper room had windows that opened toward Jerusalem.
Daniel opened these windows.
Three times every day, Daniel knelt down.
He prayed to his God.
He gave thanks to his God.
Daniel did this just as he had always done before.
passages.original: וְ֠דָנִיֵּאל כְּדִ֨י יְדַ֜ע דִּֽי־ רְשִׁ֤ים כְּתָבָא֙ עַ֣ל לְבַיְתֵ֔הּ וְכַוִּ֨ין פְּתִיחָ֥ן לֵהּ֙ בְּעִלִּיתֵ֔הּ נֶ֖גֶד יְרוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וְזִמְנִין֩ תְּלָתָ֨ה בְיוֹמָ֜א ה֣וּא׀ בָּרֵ֣ךְ עַל־ בִּרְכ֗וֹהִי וּמְצַלֵּ֤א וּמוֹדֵא֙ קֳדָ֣ם אֱלָהֵ֔הּ כָּל־ קֳבֵל֙ דִּֽי־ הֲוָ֣א עָבֵ֔ד מִן־ קַדְמַ֖ת דְּנָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then these men went as a group and found Daniel petitioning and imploring his God.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a faithful servant of God.
He was an exile from Judah.
King Darius had signed a decree.
The decree forbade prayer to anyone except the king for thirty days.
A group of men watched Daniel.
These men went together to Daniel’s house.
They found Daniel praying.
Daniel was asking and pleading with his God.
passages.original: אֱ֠דַיִן גֻּבְרַיָּ֤א אִלֵּךְ֙ הַרְגִּ֔שׁוּ וְהַשְׁכַּ֖חוּ לְדָנִיֵּ֑אל בָּעֵ֥א וּמִתְחַנַּ֖ן קֳדָ֥ם אֱלָהֵֽהּ׃

passages.text: So they approached the king and asked about his royal decree: “Did you not sign a decree that for thirty days any man who petitions any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions?” The king replied, “According to the law of the Medes and Persians the order stands, and it cannot be repealed.”
passages.sermon:
The men went to the king.
They spoke to the king about his royal decree.
They said, “O king, you signed a decree.
The decree says that for thirty days, any person who prays to any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.”
The king answered them.
He said, “The order stands.
It is the law of the Medes and Persians.
This law cannot be changed.”
passages.original: בֵּ֠אדַיִן קְרִ֨יבוּ וְאָמְרִ֥ין קֳדָם־ מַלְכָּא֮ עַל־ אֱסָ֣ר מַלְכָּא֒ הֲלָ֧א אֱסָ֣ר רְשַׁ֗מְתָּ דִּ֣י כָל־ אֱנָ֡שׁ דִּֽי־ יִבְעֵה֩ מִן־ כָּל־ אֱלָ֨הּ וֶֽאֱנָ֜שׁ עַד־ יוֹמִ֣ין תְּלָתִ֗ין לָהֵן֙ מִנָּ֣ךְ מַלְכָּ֔א יִתְרְמֵ֕א לְג֖וֹב אַרְיָותָ֑א עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֗ר יַצִּיבָ֧א מִלְּתָ֛א כְּדָת־ מָדַ֥י וּפָרַ֖ס דִּי־ לָ֥א תֶעְדֵּֽא׃

passages.text: Then they told the king, “Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, shows no regard for you, O king, or for the decree that you have signed. He still makes his petition three times a day.”
passages.sermon:
Daniel was one of the exiles from Judah.
The men spoke to the king about Daniel.
They said Daniel does not show regard for you, O king.
They said Daniel does not respect the decree you have signed.
Daniel still prays three times every day.
Daniel continues to make his petition to his God.
passages.original: בֵּ֠אדַיִן עֲנ֣וֹ וְאָמְרִין֮ קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּא֒ דִּ֣י דָנִיֵּ֡אל דִּי֩ מִן־ בְּנֵ֨י גָלוּתָ֜א דִּ֣י יְה֗וּד לָא־ שָׂ֨ם עֲלַיִךְ מַלְכָּא֙ טְעֵ֔ם וְעַל־ אֱסָרָ֖א דִּ֣י רְשַׁ֑מְתָּ וְזִמְנִ֤ין תְּלָתָה֙ בְּיוֹמָ֔א בָּעֵ֖א בָּעוּתֵֽהּ׃

passages.text: As soon as the king heard this, he was deeply distressed and set his mind on delivering Daniel, and he labored until sundown to rescue him.
passages.sermon:
King Darius ruled the Medes and Persians.
He made a law that could not be changed.
The king heard that Daniel broke this law.
The king became very upset.
He cared about Daniel.
He decided to try to save Daniel.
The king worked hard all day to rescue Daniel.
He tried until the sun went down.
passages.original: אֱדַ֨יִן מַלְכָּ֜א כְּדִ֧י מִלְּתָ֣א שְׁמַ֗ע שַׂגִּיא֙ בְּאֵ֣שׁ עֲל֔וֹהִי וְעַ֧ל דָּנִיֵּ֛אל שָׂ֥ם בָּ֖ל לְשֵׁיזָבוּתֵ֑הּ וְעַד֙ מֶֽעָלֵ֣י שִׁמְשָׁ֔א הֲוָ֥א מִשְׁתַּדַּ֖ר לְהַצָּלוּתֵֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then the men approached the king together and said to him, “Remember, O king, that by the law of the Medes and Persians no decree or ordinance established by the king can be changed.”
passages.sermon:
The men came together.
They approached the king.
They spoke to the king.
They said, “O king, remember this law.
The law is from the Medes and Persians.
No decree or ordinance that the king establishes can be changed.”
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֙יִן֙ גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֔ךְ הַרְגִּ֖שׁוּ עַל־ מַלְכָּ֑א וְאָמְרִ֣ין לְמַלְכָּ֗א דַּ֤ע מַלְכָּא֙ דִּֽי־ דָת֙ לְמָדַ֣י וּפָרַ֔ס דִּֽי־ כָל־ אֱסָ֥ר וּקְיָ֛ם דִּֽי־ מַלְכָּ֥א יְהָקֵ֖ים לָ֥א לְהַשְׁנָיָֽה׃

passages.text: So the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions. The king said to Daniel, “May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you!”
passages.sermon:
King Darius ruled the Medes and Persians.
King Darius gave an order about Daniel.
The king’s servants brought Daniel to him.
They threw Daniel into the den of lions.
King Darius spoke to Daniel.
King Darius said, “Daniel, you serve your God all the time.”
King Darius said, “May your God deliver you.”
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֜יִן מַלְכָּ֣א אֲמַ֗ר וְהַיְתִיו֙ לְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל וּרְמ֕וֹ לְגֻבָּ֖א דִּ֣י אַרְיָוָתָ֑א עָנֵ֤ה מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָמַ֣ר לְדָנִיֵּ֔אל אֱלָהָ֗ךְ דִּ֣י אַנְתָּה פָּֽלַֽח־ לֵהּ֙ בִּתְדִירָ֔א ה֖וּא יְשֵׁיזְבִנָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the rings of his nobles, so that nothing concerning Daniel could be changed.
passages.sermon:
The king of the Medes and Persians gave an order about Daniel.
Men brought a stone.
They placed the stone over the mouth of the lions’ den.
The king sealed the stone with his own signet ring.
The king’s nobles also sealed it with their rings.
No one could change what was done to Daniel.
passages.original: וְהֵיתָ֙יִת֙ אֶ֣בֶן חֲדָ֔ה וְשֻׂמַ֖ת עַל־ פֻּ֣ם גֻּבָּ֑א וְחַתְמַ֨הּ מַלְכָּ֜א בְּעִזְקְתֵ֗הּ וּבְעִזְקָת֙ רַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי דִּ֛י לָא־ תִשְׁנֵ֥א צְב֖וּ בְּדָנִיֵּֽאל׃

passages.text: Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting. No entertainment was brought before him, and sleep fled from him.
passages.sermon:
King Darius was the ruler.
He went back to his palace.
He did not eat that night.
He fasted all night.
No one brought him entertainment.
He could not sleep.
Sleep left him.
passages.original: אֱ֠דַיִן אֲזַ֨ל מַלְכָּ֤א לְהֵֽיכְלֵהּ֙ וּבָ֣ת טְוָ֔ת וְדַחֲוָ֖ן לָא־ הַנְעֵ֣ל קָֽדָמ֑וֹהִי וְשִׁנְתֵּ֖הּ נַדַּ֥ת עֲלֽוֹהִי׃

passages.text: At the first light of dawn, the king got up and hurried to the den of lions.
passages.sermon:
The king ruled over the land.
\r\nHe cared about Daniel.
\r\nMorning came.
\r\nThe sun began to rise.
\r\nThe king got up early.
\r\nHe moved quickly.
\r\nHe hurried to the lions’ den.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֣יִן מַלְכָּ֔א בִּשְׁפַּרְפָּרָ֖א יְק֣וּם בְּנָגְהָ֑א וּבְהִ֨תְבְּהָלָ֔ה לְגֻבָּ֥א דִֽי־ אַרְיָוָתָ֖א אֲזַֽל׃

passages.text: When he reached the den, he cried out in a voice of anguish, “O Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to deliver you from the lions?”
passages.sermon:
King Darius cared deeply for Daniel.
King Darius hurried to the lions’ den at dawn.
King Darius reached the den where Daniel was.
King Darius called out with a troubled voice.
King Darius cried out in anguish.
King Darius spoke to Daniel.
King Darius said, “Daniel, you serve the living God.
You serve your God faithfully and continually.
Has your God been able to save you from the lions?”
passages.original: וּכְמִקְרְבֵ֣הּ לְגֻבָּ֔א לְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל בְּקָ֥ל עֲצִ֖יב זְעִ֑ק עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֣ר לְדָנִיֵּ֗אל דָּֽנִיֵּאל֙ עֲבֵד֙ אֱלָהָ֣א חַיָּ֔א אֱלָהָ֗ךְ דִּ֣י אַנְתָּה פָּֽלַֽח־ לֵהּ֙ בִּתְדִירָ֔א הַיְכִ֥ל לְשֵׁיזָבוּתָ֖ךְ מִן־ אַרְיָוָתָֽא׃

passages.text: Then Daniel replied, “O king, may you live forever!
passages.sermon: Daniel was a faithful servant of God.\r\nDaniel spoke to the king.\r\nDaniel said, "O king, may you live forever!"
passages.original: אֱדַ֙יִן֙ דָּנִיֶּ֔אל עִם־ מַלְכָּ֖א מַלִּ֑ל מַלְכָּ֖א לְעָלְמִ֥ין חֱיִֽי׃

passages.text: My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions. They have not hurt me, for I was found innocent in His sight, and I have done no wrong against you, O king.”
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a servant of the living God.
Daniel spoke to King Darius.
Daniel said, "My God sent His angel."
The angel shut the mouths of the lions.
The lions did not hurt me.
God found me innocent before Him.
O king, I have done no wrong against you."
passages.original: אֱלָהִ֞י שְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאֲכֵ֗הּ וּֽסֲגַ֛ר פֻּ֥ם אַרְיָוָתָ֖א וְלָ֣א חַבְּל֑וּנִי כָּל־ קֳבֵ֗ל דִּ֤י קָֽדָמ֙וֹהִי֙ זָכוּ֙ הִשְׁתְּכַ֣חַת לִ֔י וְאַ֤ף קָדָמַיִךְ מַלְכָּ֔א חֲבוּלָ֖ה לָ֥א עַבְדֵֽת׃

passages.text: The king was overjoyed and gave orders to lift Daniel out of the den, and when Daniel was lifted out of the den, no wounds whatsoever were found on him, because he had trusted in his God.
passages.sermon:
King Darius saw that Daniel was safe.
King Darius felt great joy.
King Darius gave a command.
He ordered his servants to lift Daniel out of the lions’ den.
The servants lifted Daniel out of the den.
They examined Daniel.
They found no wounds on Daniel.
Daniel had trusted in his God.
God kept Daniel safe.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֣יִן מַלְכָּ֗א שַׂגִּיא֙ טְאֵ֣ב עֲל֔וֹהִי וּלְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל אֲמַ֖ר לְהַנְסָקָ֣ה מִן־ גֻּבָּ֑א וְהֻסַּ֨ק דָּנִיֵּ֜אל מִן־ גֻּבָּ֗א וְכָל־ חֲבָל֙ לָא־ הִשְׁתְּכַ֣ח בֵּ֔הּ דִּ֖י הֵימִ֥ן בֵּאלָהֵֽהּ׃

passages.text: At the command of the king, the men who had falsely accused Daniel were brought and thrown into the den of lions—they and their children and wives. And before they had reached the bottom of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
passages.sermon:
King Darius gave a command.
The king ordered the men who had falsely accused Daniel to be brought.
The king ordered these men to be thrown into the lions’ den.
The king also ordered their children and wives to be thrown into the den.
The lions’ den was a place where hungry lions lived.
The men, their children, and their wives were thrown into the den together.
They did not reach the bottom of the den.
The lions overpowered them before they reached the bottom.
The lions crushed all their bones.
passages.original: וַאֲמַ֣ר מַלְכָּ֗א וְהַיְתִ֞יו גֻּבְרַיָּ֤א אִלֵּךְ֙ דִּֽי־ אֲכַ֤לוּ קַרְצ֙וֹהִי֙ דִּ֣י דָֽנִיֵּ֔אל וּלְגֹ֤ב אַרְיָוָתָא֙ רְמ֔וֹ אִנּ֖וּן בְּנֵיה֣וֹן וּנְשֵׁיה֑וֹן וְלָֽא־ מְט֞וֹ לְאַרְעִ֣ית גֻּבָּ֗א עַ֠ד דִּֽי־ שְׁלִ֤טֽוּ בְהוֹן֙ אַרְיָ֣וָתָ֔א וְכָל־ גַּרְמֵיה֖וֹן הַדִּֽקוּ׃

passages.text: Then King Darius wrote to the people of every nation and language throughout the land: “May your prosperity abound.
passages.sermon:
King Darius was the ruler at that time.
He wrote a message.
He sent this message to all people in his kingdom.
He sent it to every nation.
He sent it to every group of people.
He sent it to every language spoken in the land.
He said, “May your prosperity abound.”
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֜יִן דָּרְיָ֣וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֗א כְּ֠תַב לְֽכָל־ עַֽמְמַיָּ֞א אֻמַיָּ֧א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּ֛א דִּֽי־ דָאֲרִין בְּכָל־ אַרְעָ֖א שְׁלָמְכ֥וֹן יִשְׂגֵּֽא׃

passages.text: I hereby decree that in every part of my kingdom, men are to tremble in fear before the God of Daniel: For He is the living God, and He endures forever; His kingdom will never be destroyed, and His dominion will never end.
passages.sermon:
King Darius made a decree.
He ruled over a great kingdom.
He commanded all people in his kingdom.
He said, “Everyone must fear and tremble before the God of Daniel.
Daniel’s God is the living God.
He lives forever.
His kingdom will never be destroyed.
His rule will never end.”
passages.original: מִן־ קֳדָמַי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒ דִּ֣י׀ בְּכָל־ שָׁלְטָ֣ן מַלְכוּתִ֗י לֶהֱוֺ֤ן זָאֲעִין וְדָ֣חֲלִ֔ין מִן־ קֳדָ֖ם אֱלָהֵ֣הּ דִּי־ דָֽנִיֵּ֑אל דִּי־ ה֣וּא׀ אֱלָהָ֣א חַיָּ֗א וְקַיָּם֙ לְעָ֣לְמִ֔ין וּמַלְכוּתֵהּ֙ דִּֽי־ לָ֣א תִתְחַבַּ֔ל וְשָׁלְטָנֵ֖הּ עַד־ סוֹפָֽא׃

passages.text: He delivers and rescues; He performs signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth, for He has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions.”
passages.sermon:
God is the living God.
God delivers people.
God rescues people.
God does signs in heaven.
God does wonders on earth.
God saved Daniel.
God rescued Daniel from the lions.
passages.original: מְשֵׁיזִ֣ב וּמַצִּ֗ל וְעָבֵד֙ אָתִ֣ין וְתִמְהִ֔ין בִּשְׁמַיָּ֖א וּבְאַרְעָ֑א דִּ֚י שֵׁיזִ֣יב לְדָֽנִיֵּ֔אל מִן־ יַ֖ד אַרְיָוָתָֽא׃

passages.text: So Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a servant of God.
Daniel lived in Babylon.
Darius was king.
Cyrus the Persian was also king after Darius.
Daniel prospered while Darius ruled.
Daniel also prospered while Cyrus the Persian ruled.
passages.original: וְדָנִיֵּ֣אל דְּנָ֔ה הַצְלַ֖ח בְּמַלְכ֣וּת דָּרְיָ֑וֶשׁ וּבְמַלְכ֖וּת כּ֥וֹרֶשׁ פָּרְסָיָא׃פ
